newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT 97 net seen to rise despite Q1 drop.
newsitem.headline: PLDT 97 net seen to rise despite Q1 drop.

text.p: Stronger demand and a new tariff structure should boost Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co profits this year despite a dip in the first quarter, analysts said on Monday.
The Philippines' dominant telecommunications firm blamed redundancy payments for the 1.8 percent drop in profits in the first three months of the year to 1.28 billion pesos ($48.67 million).
"There's no reason to be alarmed. Their net operating income was up strongly by 20 percent," said Louie Hilado at ING Baring Securities.

"We are still looking at a projected net income of 7.8 billion pesos before preferred shares for the year provided that PLDT will get its rate rebalancing approved by the second half of this year," Hilado added.
The firm's operating income for the first quarter of 1997 rose to 2.83 billion pesos from 2.36 billion.
PLDT said that without the redundancy costs, profits would have risen 17.5 percent.
Nearly 3,000 employees have left the company after the redundancy programme was started two years ago.

"The redundancy programme is a necessary cost for long term growth. PLDT is still on track. We expect them to meet our 6.1 billion peso net income projection," said Patricia Wycoco, analyst at All Asia Securities.

As part of its "rate rebalancing" plan, PLDT has asked the National Telecommunications Commission to increase basic local phone charges, lower international toll rates and implement a metering scheme for local calls to make up for the reduction in international call rates.

"If the rate rebalancing happens by the second half of the year, then they will meet our income expectations. If not, then there will be a downgrade," said Alexis Cabel, analyst at Angping & Associates Securities Inc.
Analysts said the reduction in first quarter earnings do not yet merit a downgrade in income projections, most projecting a 14 to 17 percent climb in profits for the year.

Anscor-Hagedorn Securities Inc analyst Russell Ong said projecting PLDT's earnings is proving to be difficult since the National Telecommunications Commission has yet to decide on the company's proposed rate structure.
At present, PLDT charges a monthly flat rate for local phone service regardless of number and length of calls.
PLDT closed 10 pesos lower at 1,545 pesos on the Philippine Stock Exchange in what analysts said was a knee-jerk reaction to the decline in first quarter figures.

Most analysts were pinning their hopes on PLDT's first quarter earnings to lift the stock market out of its recent downturn on the back of fears of a property glut and its impact on the banking sector. Conversion ($1=26.3 pesos)
